clue.text: Bow, having cut short nonsense

indicators.note: cutting something short trims its end, so the last letter of the nonsense word goes

parts.note: fiddlesticks is an old exclamation meaning nonsense

explanation.surface: A violinist's bow has been trimmed, and someone dismisses the whole affair as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddlestick is the bow used to play a violin, the instrument informally called a fiddle.

clue.text: Plan one beloved king ignored

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the king is left out, so his letter is dropped from the word for beloved

parts.note: dear means beloved
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: A scheme in which one dear monarch is passed over.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a plan or scheme someone has thought up.

clue.text: Lacking energy, had a go at turning over soil

indicators.note: turning over flips the remaining letters so they read backwards in this down entry
lacking energy means the letter for energy is taken away

parts.note: tried means had a go at
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tired gardener half-heartedly attempts to dig over the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking' removes E from TRIED, leaving TRID, and 'turning over' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt is loose earth, a common synonym for soil.

clue.text: What's written after passing rubbish heap outside mine

indicators.note: outside says the jumbled letters sit around the word for mine
rubbish as an adjective means poor, signalling the letters of heap are in a bad state and reordered

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A scene of a spoil heap beside a mine, as if describing a colliery landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' here means dying, not walking by, so the definition is a tombstone inscription.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is the inscription on a tombstone, composed in memory of someone who has died.

clue.text: Spiritless team thrashed

indicators.note: thrashed suggests something beaten about, so the four letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports report on a dispirited side that was heavily beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Tame describes something dull and lacking spirit or excitement.

clue.text: Overcome hard nut, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means the word is heard rather than read, so it is a sound-alike

parts.note: a conker is the hard nut of the horse chestnut tree, used in a British children's game

explanation.surface: Someone tackles a tough problem, a hard nut to crack, and is said to have beaten it.
explanation.walkthrough: A conker is a horse chestnut, threaded on string for a British playground game.
explanation.definitionFit: To conquer is to defeat or get the better of something.

clue.text: Large carnivore's frightful, we hear, to tolerate

indicators.note: we hear marks a sound-alike of the word for frightful

parts.note: grisly means gruesome or frightful
to bear is to tolerate

explanation.surface: A big meat-eater is described as dreadful and hard to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: The grizzly is a large North American brown bear, a meat-eating predator.

clue.text: Prickly shrub surrounding a river bank in underwater structure

indicators.note: surrounding says the shrub's letters go round the next pieces

parts.note: brier, or briar, is a thorny shrub
R is the map abbreviation for river
a reef is a ridge or bank of rock or sand in the sea

explanation.surface: A thorny bush grows round a river bank, oddly placed in something below the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great Barrier Reef, off Australia, is the best-known example.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier reef is a long coral ridge lying offshore, separated from land by a lagoon.

clue.text: Waste found in area by northern river

indicators.note: by means next to, so the area letter is set beside the river

parts.note: the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Pollution is discovered near a river in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is the nitrogen-rich compound by which the body excretes waste, chiefly in urine.

clue.text: Troublesome current item: finding new employees

indicators.note: troublesome letters are unruly, so they are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An awkward item on the agenda at the moment is the search for staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Recruitment is the process of hiring people to fill jobs.

clue.text: Last letter in vehicle for emperor

indicators.note: in places the final letter of the alphabet inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The final letter arrives in a carriage fit for a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Czar, also tsar, was the title of the Russian emperor.

clue.text: Heroic trips organised before records were kept

indicators.note: organised letters are arranged afresh, so these are reordered

explanation.surface: Brave expeditions were arranged in an age before anyone wrote things down.
explanation.definitionFit: Prehistoric refers to the time before written history began.

clue.text: Nod fiercely, surprisingly in environmental harmony

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone nods vigorously, unexpectedly showing agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Eco-friendly describes products or practices that do not harm nature.

clue.text: Right part sent back — time to find proof of purchase

indicators.note: sent back means the word for part is read in reverse

parts.note: a piece is a part

explanation.surface: A faulty component is returned, and the customer needs the paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is the slip given to a buyer confirming payment.

clue.text: Symbolic number accepting fine

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for fine goes inside the number

parts.note: ten is a number
OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: A figure takes on a penalty as a gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: A token gesture is a symbolic one, made for show rather than effect.

clue.text: Decide to crack this crossword again?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to solve once more

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into RE (again) plus SOLVE (crack the puzzle).
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve on something is to make up one's mind, while split up it means to work out a puzzle anew.

clue.text: Fishing equipment rocks!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the winding drums on fishing rods
second meaning: to reel is to stagger or sway

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks!' reads like praise for the kit, but it is the verb meaning sways.
explanation.definitionFit: Reels are the line-winding devices on rods, and someone who reels sways unsteadily.

clue.text: Hang about in seaside resort before run

indicators.note: before puts the resort ahead of the run letter

parts.note: Hove is a seaside town on the south coast of England, next to Brighton
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone loiters at the coast before going for a jog.
explanation.definitionFit: To hover is to linger or wait around near a place.

clue.text: Occasionally shout very loudly in fit of anger

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only alternate letters of the word are kept

parts.note: FF, fortissimo, is the musical notation for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone bellows now and then while in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of SHOUT give HU.
explanation.definitionFit: A huff is a sulky bout of annoyance or pique.

clue.text: Alpine transport except after end of snowmelt

indicators.note: after places the word for except following that letter
end of picks the final letter of the word

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: Mountain lifts stop running once the snow melts away.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bar is a ski lift with T-shaped bars that tow skiers uphill.

clue.text: With change of top, stomach is wobbly!

indicators.note: a change of top means the first letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: belly means stomach

explanation.surface: An exclamation that someone's tummy is quivering.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of BELLY is replaced, giving a word for a wobbly dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Jelly, the set dessert, is famous for shaking, so it stands for something that wobbles.

clue.text: Resentful of Jack, a six-footer cycling

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end to the other

parts.note: a louse is an insect, which has six legs

explanation.surface: Someone is bitter towards Jack, a tall man out on his bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person but means an insect with six feet; ALOUSE, cycled, puts its final E at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealous means envious or resentful of another's advantages.

clue.text: Distance, for example, a cart must reverse

indicators.note: must reverse means the string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a dray is a low cart for heavy loads

explanation.surface: A wagon must back up some way, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardage is a distance measured in yards, as in American football or golf.

clue.text: Make firm points to clinch argument

indicators.note: to clinch is to grip tightly, so the compass letters hold the argument inside

parts.note: S, E and N are compass points: south, east, north
a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone makes several points to win a debate.
explanation.definitionFit: To stiffen is to make rigid or harden.

clue.text: Link part of South American custom

parts.note: usage means custom or habitual practice

explanation.surface: A connection is drawn to part of a South American tradition.
explanation.walkthrough: Sausages come in a chain of links, so one link is a single sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A sausage link is one of a string of connected sausages.

clue.text: Has some downsides

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the letters sit inside the word

explanation.surface: An admission that something comes with a few drawbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to have or possess it.

clue.text: Editor with deal, oddly, for literary collection

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd positions of the word

explanation.surface: An editor strikes a strange deal for an anthology.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is a medieval Icelandic compilation of Norse myths and poetry.

clue.text: Celebrated wildebeests turning up

indicators.note: turning up in a down entry reads the word from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: gnus are wildebeests

explanation.surface: Antelopes are cheered as they arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Sung as in sung of or praised: celebrated in song, as in the phrase unsung heroes.

clue.text: Piercing lamentation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as in sharp or penetrating
second meaning: an Irish wailing lament for the dead

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as a shrill cry, but each is a separate sense of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen means sharp, as of a wind or blade, and is also a noun for a mournful funeral wail.

clue.text: Surprisingly outraged don's benevolent

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A university lecturer who was furious turns out, unexpectedly, to be kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for is, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-natured means kindly and well-disposed towards others.

clue.text: Man perhaps lies badly

indicators.note: badly means poorly done, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A man, it seems, is a poor liar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island, which is what the word names.

clue.text: English country squire welcomes a property dealer

indicators.note: welcomes means taking in a guest, so the letter A goes inside the chain of pieces

parts.note: a state is a country or nation
a gent, short for gentleman, is a squire

explanation.surface: An English country landowner receives a visitor who deals in houses.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate agent is the British term for someone who sells or lets homes, a realtor.
